subject: ventures/open-tennis-robots
professional: a sports-biomechanics/ballistics engineer who builds ball machines, plus a robotics safety engineer (machine guarding, e-stop, ISO 13849 thinking) who would sign off the firmware safety claims

evidence.correctness: Ran `tennisbots aim --x 9 --y -2 --speed 22 --topspin 1200` (elev 19.57, az -5.34, clearance 1.89 m, flight 1.30 s, wheels 4367/2223 rpm). Recomputed independently: (1) a separate pure-Python midpoint integrator at dt=1e-5 with the same published drag/Magnus-fit constants landed at (9.003, -1.999), clearance 1.887 m, t=1.2996 s: matches. (2) No-drag 20 m/s at 30 deg: sim range 35.3119 m vs closed form v^2 sin(2a)/g = 35.3119 m, flight time 2.03874 vs 2.03874 s. (3) Wheel rpm by hand: total 2*22/0.85=51.76, diff 2*0.0335*125.66/0.5=16.84, vt 34.30, vb 17.46 m/s -> 4367/2223 rpm. (4) Court constants vs ITF: 23.77, 8.23, 10.97, net 0.914/1.07, posts 0.914 outside doubles line (6.399) all correct. (5) README catch table cells re-run with --n 300 --seed 1: 1.5 m 19%/80%, 3.0 m 31%/91% exactly as published. Not checked: bounce model against measured data, CAD package geometry (build123d not installed here).
evidence.completeness: Checked claims: Python package (flight, aim, drill, tracker, catcher, collector, drive, vision, protocol, listing) all present and CLI subcommands aim/drill/catch-study/collect ran end to end; ESP32 controller+protocol present; browser sim.mjs port passes its 21 node tests; collector and feeder manufacturing packages and BOMs exist on disk; README states honestly no robot is built and lists what the feeder CAD omits. Stub-ish: firmware set_base on the collector is `pass` (by role), `drive` on feeder `pass`; the feed interlock exists in main.py:180 but only on hardware. Not verified: CAD regeneration and 'CI fails if package stale' (no build123d), live page (proxy 403). Roadmap items 3-9 are openly not done.
evidence.verification: Python: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> 38 tests OK (pytest not installed). Node: `node --test sim.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs` -> 21 pass. Mutation 1: Magnus lift constant in ballistics.lift_coeff `2.0 -> 2.6` (~15-20% less lift): all 38 Python tests and the JS tests still passed (survived). Mutation 2: catcher.CatchRig.catches half-width test `net_width/2 -> net_width` (net effectively twice as wide): all 38 tests passed (survived); only a loose 'moving beats fixed' test touches the catch path, and no test pins a catch rate or the net geometry. Both reverted with git checkout; tree clean. Good tests exist for vacuum closed form, bounce energy, firmware watchdog/e-stop/bumper, but core numeric outputs are not pinned to values.
evidence.craft: Read ballistics.py, launcher.py, catcher.py, court.py, firmware/esp32/controller.py. Clean, typed, documented with units and frames; RK4 integrator; bracketing+bisection aim with azimuth correction; controller touches hardware only via `hw` so it is testable on CPython. Defects: firmware set_base forwards the target unclamped (no rail limit, controller.py SET_BASE branch); Flight.crossing and aim iteration have silent fallbacks (aim loop exits after 6 passes without error if not converged); study() cost is high (300x4 cells took ~90 s for 4 cells); the JS sim is a second copy of the physics kept in sync only by fixtures; spin decay in flight is ignored (documented).
evidence.claims: Backed: catch table (reproduced), 'no simulated return cleared a 2.5 m frame' (too_high 0%), MIT/sell guide, no-warranty text on README/safety.md, ITF constants, feed interlock (firmware/esp32/main.py:181), bumper reverse-only (test). Unbacked or overstated: safety.md says 'wheel rpm, aim angles, base speed and drive speed are clamped whatever the Pi sends' but base POSITION is not clamped or rail-limited in firmware, and the interlock/main.py hardware layer has no tests; safety.md/README imply a latching e-stop but a software CLEAR_ESTOP from the Pi re-arms once the button is released, with no human reset step; llms.txt 'Browser demo' and pyproject Homepage point at the old duncan-haywood.github.io address rather than marisstella.app (redirect only). Launcher efficiencies (0.85 speed, 0.5 spin) and the club-player return distribution are guesses, flagged as such in README, but the headline 91% catch figure rests on them.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a builder wanting to land a ball machine shot or size a net can run aim/catch-study and get plausible, self-consistent numbers; a builder of the collector has a full DXF/STL/STEP/BOM package. But nothing has been built or bench-tested, the launcher calibration and return distribution are unvalidated, feeder CAD omits netting, agitator, actuator brackets and azimuth drive, and a safety-critical firmware gap (unclamped base target, software e-stop clear) means a builder cannot yet trust it to run next to people. A tinkerer could start; a seller could not ship.
evidence.domain: Compared against the sports-physics literature the module cites (Mehta/Nathan style C_L = 1/(2+v/(r*omega)), constant C_d ~0.55, friction-limited bounce with COR 0.75, ITF ball mass and radius, two-wheel launcher exit speed = mean surface speed times slip efficiency, topspin from top wheel faster). Method is standard and the sign conventions check out (top wheel faster gives topspin; Magnus force down). Departures: constant C_d (no Reynolds dependence), no in-flight spin decay, single-parameter friction bounce with no court-surface variants, tracker ignores unknown spin which README admits is the main error source. A robotics safety engineer would want a risk assessment, a hardware-level e-stop reset that cannot be software cleared, and a rail-limit in firmware.

defects.what: Mutating the catch-width test (net half-width doubled) leaves all 38 Python and 21 JS tests green; no test pins a catch rate, net geometry, or the Magnus lift constant (changed by 30% also survived). The README's headline numbers are unprotected from regression.
Firmware SET_BASE passes the lateral target through unclamped, so a bad Pi command can drive the base beyond the rail; safety.md says base limits are enforced in firmware.
Software CLEAR_ESTOP from the Pi re-arms the machine whenever the physical button is not pressed; a safety reviewer expects a deliberate local reset.
Feed interlock (wheels within 5% of target) lives only in hardware-bound main.py and is untested; safety.md leans on it.
llms.txt and pyproject point to the old duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of marisstella.app.
aim() exits its azimuth-correction loop after 6 passes without signalling non-convergence; README catch study takes ~90 s for four cells.

verdict: Physics and planners are right where checked: an independent integrator, closed-form vacuum range, hand-computed wheel speeds, ITF constants and the published catch table all reproduce, and the README is unusually honest that nothing is built and the distributions are guesses. It does not meet the bar because verification is weak (two seeded bugs, including a doubled net width and a 30% change in Magnus lift, passed every test) and a safety claim over-reaches the firmware (unclamped base target, software e-stop clear). Finished in scope for a v0.1 design, but not something a robotics safety engineer would sign off for people-adjacent use.
